title: TypeScript SDK: ergonomic primitives for AsyncIterable <-> Web Streams interop
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: TypeScript SDK users face friction when wiring server streaming responses into browser Web Streams or Node AsyncIterables. Current SDK has multiple ad-hoc helpers across repos and inconsistent cancellation/backpressure semantics. Goal: provide a small, well-tested set of ergonomic primitives and examples that make AsyncIterable <-> ReadableStream interop reliable, cancellable, and retry-friendly. Deliverables: 1) API surface: lightweight helper APIs (toAsyncIterable, toReadableStream, streamCollector, streamCheckpoint) with clear semantics for backpressure and cancellation. 2) Retry-aware streaming fn: helper that composes resumable retries for idempotent streaming requests (checkpoint token + partial-offset replay). 3) Examples and migration guide: idiomatic browser and Node examples, cookbook for common patterns (fan-out, multi-consume, graceful reconnect). 4) Tests and benchmarks: round-trip latency, throughput, and memory under large concurrent streams. 5) Docs and release notes.
acceptance_criteria: New helpers exported from @redwood/sdk-streams with types and JSDoc
Helpers correctly convert between AsyncIterable<Uint8Array|string> and ReadableStream in Node and browser environments (without depending on global polyfills by default)
Cancellation from consumer side propagates to underlying request and frees runtime resources within 50ms in benchmarks
Resumable retry helper can resume from a checkpoint token without duplicating already-delivered tokens (end-to-end integration test)
Examples for: browser fetch -> ReadableStream -> toAsyncIterable; Node readable stream -> toReadableStream -> fetch-like client; combined with retry helper
Unit and integration tests cover error propagation, backpressure semantics, and memory regressions
PRs reviewed and merged with accompanying CHANGELOG entry and migration notes
design_notes: Core primitives are intentionally minimal and implementation-focused: toAsyncIterable(stream), toReadableStream(iterable), streamCollector(iterable, options), resumableStreamFetch(url, opts)

Backpressure: toAsyncIterable should await stream.getReader().read() and yield each chunk; toReadableStream should use start(controller) with a pull() that pulls next() from the iterator and enqueue()s. Ensure highWaterMark tuning is exposed via options.

Cancellation: use AbortController semantics. All helpers accept an optional AbortSignal and must call underlying cancel/close methods when signaled. In Node, prefer ReadableStream.cancel(); in browser use reader.releaseLock + controller.close patterns as appropriate.

Retries/resume: server will return checkpoint tokens (opaque string) in streaming metadata chunks. resumableStreamFetch composes initial request -> stream consumption -> if transient network error and server supports resume token, re-issue request with resume token header and continue yielding new chunks. Deduplication is done client-side by tracking last-seen sequence id per-shard when available.
Type ergonomics: provide narrow exported types (StreamLike = AsyncIterable<Uint8Array|string>|ReadableStream<Uint8Array|string>) and helper overloads so callers get good inference in TS projects.

Polyfills: do not include Web Stream polyfills by default. Provide small runtime-detection helpers and an optional import @redwood/sdk-streams/polyfills to enable older runtimes. Document Node 18+ recommended baseline.
Security: helpers do not serialize auth tokens; resumable headers are opaque and passed through. No PII handling changes.

Performance: keep copying minimal. Prefer Uint8Array chunk boundaries; only convert to string when user requests text decode via convenience overloads. Expose an experimental zero-copy mode for advanced users in a separate opt-in API.
Migration: existing ad-hoc utilities will be deprecated and re-exported as compatibility wrappers for one release cycle with console.warn to encourage migration.

Open questions: 1) canonical shape for server-provided resume metadata (header vs first-chunk JSON envelope) - decide with backend. 2) conflict resolution when multiple consumers request the same AsyncIterable (should we offer a sharedReplay utility?)
implementation_plan: Week 1: API design + types + PRD; pick names and opt-in compatibility wrappers
Week 2: implement toAsyncIterable and toReadableStream with unit tests covering Node/browser runtime detection
Week 3: implement resumableStreamFetch with integration test against a local mock streaming server that emits checkpoint tokens
Week 4: examples, benchmarks, docs, and deprecation wrappers; open PR for review
Week 5: iterate on review feedback, perf regressions, and merge; publish npm beta and release notes

tests_and_benchmarks: Unit tests: conversion helpers, cancellation propagation, backpressure scenarios (slow consumer vs fast producer)
Integration test: local mock server that streams 100k small chunks; verify memory and no duplication across resume; measure time to free resources after abort
Benchmark scripts: node-bench/run-large-stream.sh to measure tokens/sec for streaming pipeline with and without conversion helpers; target <10% overhead vs raw runtime API
E2E: browser example using fetch + ReadableStream -> toAsyncIterable consumed by application UI; measure latency from first byte to render
docs_and_examples: Migration guide: docs/migration/streams-2.3.md with compatibility table and deprecation timeline
Cookbook snippets: fan-out consumption, single-consumer shared-replay (recommended shared helper), graceful reconnect pattern using resumableStreamFetch
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: inconsistent server resume metadata format - Mitigation: work with backend team (BKEND-449) to agree on first-chunk envelope schema and include feature-flagged fallbacks
Risk: memory growth when consumers do not drain streams - Mitigation: provide diagnostics, enforce soft limits in examples, emit console warnings when internal buffer > threshold
Risk: divergence in Node/browser behavior - Mitigation: runtime detection and explicit required Node baseline in docs; optional polyfill package for older runtimes
Risk: duplicate deliveries during resume - Mitigation: require server sequence ids when resume is used; client deduplication in resumableStreamFetch
